primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic kidney disease (proteinuric chronic kidney disease)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) with TA775 for SGLT2 inhibitors

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood‑pressure control in CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203: first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NG203: add CCB if BP not at target with ACE‑I alone

medications.dose: Individualised dosing according to glucose monitoring
medications.duration: Ongoing — review at each clinic visit
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for diabetes (required for CKD management)
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management per NICE NG28 (supportive of CKD care)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and electrolytes at 2 weeks, then every 6 months
medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular risk in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 & TA775: SGLT2‑i indicated for CKD with ACR ≥ 2.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (CKD is a CVD‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: statin recommended for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increasing risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Reduce insulin dose by 10‑20 % and monitor blood glucose closely for the first 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on intravascular volume may cause hypotension or acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Check blood pressure and serum creatinine/eGFR 1‑2 weeks after initiation; ensure adequate hydration

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase statin plasma concentrations, modestly raising risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin (less affected than simvastatin) and monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention in eGFR 46 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; patient already on ACE‑I only
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone; do not add ARB

assumptions_warnings: Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not provided; protein dip‑stick suggests significant proteinuria, assumed to meet SGLT2‑i indication.
Baseline lipid profile, liver function tests, and serum potassium not available; will obtain before starting atorvastatin and monitor after dapagliflozin.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available; anemia will be investigated before prescribing iron supplementation.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑i not documented; will confirm with patient.
Blood pressure reading not recorded; target <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if proteinuria severe) will be pursued.
treatment_summary: The plan continues ACE‑I and CCB therapy, adds dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for renal protection and cardiovascular benefit, and starts atorvastatin 20 mg daily for CV risk reduction. Insulin dosing will be adjusted for the added SGLT2‑i. Monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, glucose, lipids, and CK will be performed per NG203. NSAIDs are avoided and no ACE‑I/ARB dual therapy is used.
